LESSON: CLASSIFICATION OF PLANTS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
Strand: Living Things and their Environment
Topic 1.1: Classification of Plants

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Classification of Plants. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: when handling plants as they study flowering and non- flowering plants. How are plants classified?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. classify plants into flowering and non- flowering
2. describe functions of parts of a flower
3. appreciate the importance of flowers in nature
4. describe general characteristics of vertebrates
5. classify vertebrates into their main groups

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CLASSIFICATION OF PLANTS
Subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Classification of Plants helps you succeed in SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT PLANTS
Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.
Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.
Without water and light, most seedlings wilt.

PART 1: Classify plants into flowering and non- flowering

What this means
In this part you learn to classify plants into flowering and non- flowering. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: classify plants into flowering and non- flowering.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Classification of Plants” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can classify plants into flowering and non- flowering. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe functions of parts of a flower

What this means
In this part you learn to describe functions of parts of a flower. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe functions of parts of a flower.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Classification of Plants matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe functions of parts of a flower. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the importance of flowers in nature

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of flowers in nature. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of flowers in nature.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Classification of Plants this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of flowers in nature. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Describe general characteristics of vertebrates

What this means
In this part you learn to describe general characteristics of vertebrates. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe general characteristics of vertebrates.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Classification of Plants” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe general characteristics of vertebrates. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 5: Classify vertebrates into their main groups

What this means
In this part you learn to classify vertebrates into their main groups. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: classify vertebrates into their main groups.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Classification of Plants matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can classify vertebrates into their main groups. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Classification of Plants is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.

Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Classification of Plants” around your school. (skill: classify plants into flowering and non- flowering)

Example 2: Say why Classification of Plants matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: describe functions of parts of a flower)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Classification of Plants this week. (skill: appreciate the importance of flowers in nature)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Classification of Plants” around your school. (skill: describe general characteristics of vertebrates)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Classification of Plants to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: classify plants into flowering and non- flowering.
3. Practise this skill: describe functions of parts of a flower.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of flowers in nature.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Classification of Plants from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Classification of Plants: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Classification of Plants?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when handling plants as they study flowering and non- flowering plants. How are plants classified?
2. What are the key features of vertebrates?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Classification of Plants means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: classify plants into flowering and non- flowering.
5. Be able to: describe functions of parts of a flower.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
